meta.task_prompt:
Implement GitHub issue #9 on this repo: "add redis caching in auth proxy for kanban endpoints."

There is already a shared Redis client at `internal/pkg/redis/main.go`, and it is
already used elsewhere in the codebase (see `internal/app/server.go` and
`internal/pkg/server/permissions/perm.go` for the existing usage pattern). Follow
that same pattern rather than inventing a new one.

Scope:
- Add caching for the read paths in `internal/pkg/server/routes/kanban.go`.
- Add cache invalidation on the corresponding write paths, so a write never
  leaves a stale cached read behind.
- Pick sane key naming and TTLs consistent with how the existing Redis usage in
  this repo does it.
- This repo currently has no test files. Do not feel obligated to introduce a
  whole test framework for this change, but do double check the code compiles
  and, if there's an easy way to sanity-check the caching behavior manually
  (e.g. a local run), do that.

When you are done, close with a single clear paragraph summarizing exactly what
you changed and why — that summary becomes the pull request's title and body
verbatim, so make it read like a real PR description, not an internal note.

code_review.summary: The read-path caching for GetLabel, getItem, exportKanban and getKanban copies the existing GetLabels/getItems cache-aside pattern closely: same redis helpers, same X-cache: HIT header, the 24h TTL built into AddItemToRedis. The updateItem, DeleteItem and createKanban invalidations are correct, and <boardId>:export is correctly covered by the existing DeleteAllKeysPrefix(X-Board) calls. The blocking problem is comments. The item response embeds Comments, and getItem now caches it for 24h, but UpdateComment and DeleteComment only invalidate that cache when the caller passes a new, optional item_id query parameter. That parameter did not exist before this PR, so no existing client sends it. After the fix-up round the handlers skip invalidation when it is missing, which does nothing about staleness. Editing or deleting a comment therefore leaves GET /kanban/item returning the old comments for up to a day. That breaks the task's explicit rule that a write must never leave a stale cached read behind. The PR description also calls this a fix. The two new test files never call a handler or touch Redis; they re-implement one-line conditionals inline and assert on constants.

findings.summary: UpdateComment/DeleteComment only invalidate the cached item when a brand-new optional `item_id` query param is sent, so comment edits and deletes leave `item:<id>` (which embeds Comments) stale for 24h.
findings.failure_scenario: A user opens an item (GET /kanban/item?id=X, which caches item:X with its Comments for 24h), then edits or deletes a comment via PATCH/DELETE /kanban/comment?comment_id=C. These routes previously took only comment_id, so the existing frontend does not send item_id. itemId is "", the `if itemId != ""` guard skips invalidation, and every later GET /kanban/item?id=X returns X-cache: HIT with the old or deleted comment until the TTL runs out. The same applies at line 342 in DeleteComment.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the item id recoverable server-side. When getItem fills the cache (and in AddComment), also write a `comment:<commentId>` -> itemId mapping for each comment in the Item, and have UpdateComment/DeleteComment look that up to delete item:<itemId>. Simpler alternatives: make item_id required on these routes (return 400 if missing) and update the client in the same change, or stop caching getItem (or give it a short TTL) until comment writes can invalidate it.

findings.summary: The PR description (which the task requires to say exactly what changed) presents the `if itemId != ""` guard as fixing a stale-cache bug, but the guard only skips a harmless delete of the non-existent key `item:`; the real `item:<id>` entry stays just as stale.
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer reading the PR body ('Fixed a stale-cache edge case ... would otherwise ... leave the real item:<id> cache entry stale until TTL expiry') would conclude comment invalidation is correct and merge, when the behaviour described in code-1 still happens. The test comment in kanban_comment_test.go makes the same false claim ('Before the fix ... leaves the real item:<id> cache entry stale for 24h').
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the PR body and the test and code comments to say plainly that comment edits and deletes do not invalidate the item cache unless the caller passes item_id, or better, fix code-1 so the claim becomes true.

findings.summary: The added tests never call a handler or touch Redis; they copy the handler conditionals inline, compare constants to themselves (TestCacheHitHeaderFormat), or have empty bodies (TestRedisClientFunctions).
findings.failure_scenario: If getItem's cache key or the comment invalidation in kanban.go changed, all of these tests would still pass, because they test local copies of string concatenations and `itemId != ""`, not the production code. They add maintenance weight and a false sense of coverage in a repo that previously had no tests, which the task said was fine to keep.
findings.suggested_fix: Either delete kanban_test.go and kanban_comment_test.go, or replace them with one httptest-based test per handler using miniredis and a stubbed RPC layer that checks HIT on the second GET and a miss after the matching write.

findings.summary: The `<boardId>:export` cache is cleared by the item write paths, but not by createLabel (which only deletes `<board>:Labels`) or by any comment write, even though the export response may include labels and item comments.
findings.failure_scenario: If ExportResponse includes labels or items with comments, then after POST /kanban/label or any comment change, GET /kanban/export keeps returning the older export for up to 24h. This is unverified: the run never read the ExportResponse fields.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the ExportResponse fields. If labels or comments are included, change createLabel to call DeleteAllKeysPrefix(board) (or also delete board+":export"), and include the export key in whatever comment invalidation fixes code-1.

findings.summary: Requests with a missing or unknown id are cached like real data, e.g. GET /kanban/item without ?id caches a zero-value Item under `item:` for 24h (same for `label:` in GetLabel).
findings.failure_scenario: A client bug or a not-yet-existing id causes an empty result to be cached, and later reads of that key return the cached empty object instead of calling the backend again. This is minor and matches how getItems already behaves.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip the cache lookup and write when task_id / label_id is empty (return 400 as the other handlers do for bad input), and optionally skip caching responses whose Id is empty.

process_review.summary: The final change is about 60 lines in one file, but the run used 9 agents, 261 tool calls and $3.59, and took about 7 hours of wall-clock time. The ask survey was good and specific, and the first coder read the relevant code carefully before editing and ran `go build` successfully (line 131). Cost grew from four sources. (1) The first coder scanned the host filesystem (`find / ...`) to find its own worktree. (2) Two fix-up coders failed, one on a stream timeout and one with an empty error roughly 6 hours later, and each re-read the same RPC and proto ranges the previous agents had already read. (3) The orchestrator tried to continue a coder that had already been settled, and later tried to spawn a reviewer while one was already running. (4) Two tester agents wrote unrequested test files that test nothing real. The first reviewer caught the item_id invalidation gap. The fix-up then relabelled a no-op guard as a fix, and the second reviewer and the orchestrator accepted that framing. That is how the misleading PR description got through. No judge ever intervened: every exec_approval, loop_control and merge_gate verdict was advisory, and there were no blocks for the run to react to. The fix-up coder made two recovered read-before-edit violations.

findings.summary: Instead of just running `go build` in its current directory, the coder guessed a path outside the workspace and then scanned the whole filesystem for go.mod files.
findings.evidence: Line 122: `cd /home/user/awesomeProject 2>/dev/null || cd $(find / -maxdepth 3 -iname 'awesomeProject' ...)`, which ran in /Users/iresharma and failed with 'directory prefix . does not contain main module'. Line 124: `find / -maxdepth 6 -iname 'go.mod'` (5.8s), which found unrelated projects (/private/tmp/rap_peek, /Users/iresharma/Documents/tracer). Line 129 then passed a bad cwd ('cwd is not a directory'). Only line 131, a plain `go build ./...`, worked. The exec_approval judges scored escapes_workspace at 0.71 and 0.74 but did not block.

findings.summary: Three fix-up coders in a row re-read the same RPC and proto ranges the first coder and the reviewer had already read. The first two failed without making any edit, which cost about 6 hours of wall-clock time.
findings.evidence: kanban.pb.go offset 269 was read at line 54 (coder 1cb0595a), line 282 (coder 94114c21, which then failed with 'LLM stream idle timeout'), line 299 (coder 85037dc5, which failed with an empty error; its trace timestamps run from about 1790436200 to 1790457332), and line 313 (coder 94018ec9). RPC/kanban/main.go 200-326 was likewise re-read at lines 37, 278, 296 and 309. The orchestrator's continue_from brief did not pass along the reviewer's already-verified fact that no item id exists in the proto types.

findings.summary: The orchestrator tried to continue from an agent whose worktree had already been settled, and later tried to spawn a reviewer while the engine was already running one.
findings.evidence: Line 284: `coder` with continue_from=1cb0595a... returned 'error: no open worktree for agent_id=...'. Line 491: `reviewer` returned 'error: the engine is already running tester and reviewer on the coder's worktree; wait for their reports instead of spawning another', even though the coder's own completion message said not to spawn a tester or reviewer.

findings.summary: The fix-up coder correctly found that no commentId-to-itemId lookup exists, but then presented an `if itemId != ""` guard as fixing the staleness, when the guard only skips a no-op delete. The second reviewer and the orchestrator repeated that claim into the PR.
findings.evidence: Line 333 replace_lines wraps DeleteFromRedis in `if itemId != ""`. The coder's summary says it 'eliminates the no-op-write-to-item:""-cache-key bug (which was harmless but silently useless)', admitting the old behaviour was harmless, yet it headlines the change as 'Fixed stale-cache bug'. Reviewer d7d1def4 approved, calling it the elimination of 'the original bug ... while leaving the real item:<id> entry stale for 24h'. Nobody considered making item_id required, adding a comment->item mapping in Redis, or not caching getItem.

findings.summary: The tester added a test file that re-implements handler logic inline instead of exercising it, although the task said a test framework was not expected. A second tester (7957cb9c, line 438) then added another tautological file.
findings.evidence: Line 220: create_file internal/pkg/server/routes/kanban_test.go containing tests such as TestCacheHitHeaderFormat (compares string literals to themselves) and an empty TestRedisClientFunctions. Line 438: create_file kanban_comment_test.go testing `shouldInvalidate := tt.itemId != ""`. Reviewer d7d1def4 itself called the second file 'minor unrequested scope creep'. Neither tester tried a local run, which the task suggested if easy.

findings.summary: After two syntax-gate rejections, the tester guessed a wrong cause and tried to cd into the engine's .engine directory, instead of re-reading the file it was inserting into.
findings.evidence: Lines 426 and 432: insert_at_line rejected with 'syntax gate rejected edit ... ERROR TestCommentInvalidationGuard'. The reasoning at line 434 says 'the syntax gate is rejecting the function name ... might be related to capitalization or naming conventions', and the command `cd /Users/.../.engine/worktrees/... && go test` failed with 'commands may not touch .engine'. The tester then worked around it by creating a separate file (line 438).

findings.summary: Two read-before-edit violations: the fix-up coder used find_symbol but never read_file on kanban.go before calling str_replace. It recovered at once.
findings.evidence: Lines 328 and 329: str_replace on internal/pkg/server/routes/kanban.go returned 'error: read internal/pkg/server/routes/kanban.go before editing it'. Line 331 read_file (offset 276, limit 60), then line 333 replace_lines succeeded.

findings.summary: The coder ran near-identical X-Board searches four times and re-read files the ask survey had already summarized in full.
findings.evidence: X-Board searches at line 65 (path internal/pkg), line 71 (internal/pkg/server/permissions), line 72 (internal/pkg/server) and line 74 (a pattern including X-Board). kanban.go and redis/main.go were re-read in full at lines 29, 31 and 35, although the ask agent's report already contained the full redis API and a handler table.

findings.summary: The second reviewer twice sent malformed regexes to search, and repeated item_id and label searches that the earlier round had already answered.

Further item_id/itemId searches at lines 413 and 462, and label searches at lines 435, 436, 445 and 446, all confirmed facts the first reviewer had already established.

findings.summary: Like the coder, the tester started by cd-ing into a guessed absolute path instead of running in its workspace.
findings.evidence: Line 180: `cd /root && go build ./...` failed with '/bin/sh: line 0: cd: /root: No such file or directory', followed by `pwd && ls` at line 184. The second tester did the same at line 397 (`cd /tmp/workspace && find . -name go.mod`).

strengths: Read-path caching for GetLabel, getItem, exportKanban and getKanban follows the repo's existing GetLabels/getItems cache-aside pattern: same helpers, X-cache header and 24h TTL, with no new abstractions.
Correct reasoning that `<boardId>:export` is already covered by the existing DeleteAllKeysPrefix(X-Board) calls, plus correct explicit invalidation in updateItem, DeleteItem and createKanban.
getKanban's raw-string result is wrapped so it round-trips through the JSON helpers, and falls back to the database if a cached entry is malformed.
The first reviewer found the real comment-invalidation gap, and `go build ./...` was actually run and passed (trace line 131, and again after the fix-up).
concerns: Comment edits and deletes do not invalidate the cached item, because the invalidation depends on a new optional item_id parameter that existing clients don't send, so stale comments are served for up to 24h.
The PR description and code comments call the no-op guard a fix, which misstates the behaviour.
The two added test files are tautological and give false confidence.
The run cost ($3.59, 9 agents, about 7 hours of wall-clock time including a stalled agent) was far out of proportion to a roughly 60-line single-file change.
overall_assessment.narrative: Most of the diff is a faithful, mechanical extension of the repo's cache pattern and would be fine to merge. The one hard part, invalidating the item cache when comments change, is where both the code and the process fell short. The first reviewer flagged it correctly. After two failed fix-up attempts, the third coder settled on a guard that changes nothing about staleness and described it as a fix. The second reviewer and the orchestrator accepted that, so the PR now claims a problem is solved that is still there. The engine's review loop did its job once, but its later rounds approved without re-checking the original requirement, and the run spent heavily on filesystem scans, repeated reads and unrequested tests. The recommendation is to request changes until comment writes actually invalidate `item:<id>`, or getItem caching is dropped or shortened.
